title: Trumpeters he sat under: Rex Stewart, Nesbit and others
summary: He lists the many trumpeters he played alongside, praising Rex Stewart's unorthodox fingering.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yes. Practice every day and I find that it pays off. Now, I get through working, say, 11:00 o'clock I breakneck home, get home and go to sleep. Then I wake up early, turn my records on, and listen to all these programs, jazz, and I want to hear who's playing something. And -- you see I was thrown in -- my whole life I had a list of the trumpet players that I've played with, it would take maybe three or four hours to name the trumpet players I've played with. From Joe Smith, to Rex Stewart, to the trumpet player that did all the writing for McKenna's Cotton Pickers, I forget his name, Nesbit. All these guys were different. No two guys played alike. All up the line, Rex Stewart, I thought Rex was one of the greatest -- I never saw a man play like that, without using the proper fingering of his valves. He never used proper fingering of his valves to play anything, with any valve, it didn't make any difference to him. So, I sat under these guys all of my life and I paid attention to them. All of them, everyone of them to Arthur Whetsol, Bubba Miley, Cootie Wetzel, to Bubba Marley, Cootie, Shirley Clay, Jack Hatton, Irving Ham Davis, Reverend Randolph, gosh I could sit here and name
